subject.title: Feature: Sleep/wait tool — agent can pause execution without burning tokens

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class core sleep/self-pause tool, and if so should it be a dedicated gateway resume primitive or a cron-backed session-targeted tool with explicit cap and sandbox semantics?
rationale: The request changes the model-facing core tool surface, agent turn scheduling, session continuation, and possibly config/sandbox policy, so automation should not choose the permanent product/API shape.

options.title: Sponsor a core sleep primitive
options.body: Accept the capability and require a corrected implementation with same-session resume, user-interrupt cancellation, duration cap enforcement, restart non-durability, and real behavior proof.

options.title: Keep existing cron/session guidance
options.body: Reject a new core tool for now and continue supporting delayed work through cron, background process completion wakes, and sessions_yield for spawned subagents.

options.title: Narrow to extension seam first
options.body: Ask for a plugin/runtime extension point if maintainers want optional scheduling behavior outside the default core tool surface.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a core sleep primitive
recommendation.body: Accept the capability and require a corrected implementation with same-session resume, user-interrupt cancellation, duration cap enforcement, restart non-durability, and real behavior proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main history touches the central agent tool registry, gateway/cron behavior, and docs around waits and wakes.
